title: Whisper to the Builder
story:
Excerpt from the mainland's image-scan report on `kestrel/uplink:0.9`:

`FINDING HIGH  layer 2  ARG MAINLAND_TOKEN=KP-4e9b... is readable with docker history`

The uplink build has to prove it can authenticate, so it really does need the mainland token while it builds. But the token must not survive in any layer, environment variable or history line. The token file is `/workspace/secrets/mainland.token`.

Rewrite the Dockerfile so BuildKit hands the token over as a secret, and build `kestrel/uplink:1.0`.
objectives: Rewrite `/workspace/Dockerfile` to read the token through `RUN --mount=type=secret,id=mainland_token` and drop the `ARG`
The build still wrote `token-ok` to `/opt/uplink-status`, but the token appears nowhere in the image or its history
startingState: `/workspace/Dockerfile` is the leaky version that takes the token as `ARG MAINLAND_TOKEN`; `/workspace/secrets/mainland.token` holds the token. No image has been built.
hints: Build arguments and environment variables are recorded in image metadata forever. BuildKit has a different channel: a secret is mounted for a single `RUN` step as a temporary file and leaves no trace.

In the Dockerfile, add `--mount=type=secret,id=NAME` to the `RUN` that needs it; the value appears as the file `/run/secrets/NAME`. At build time supply it with `docker build --secret id=NAME,src=FILE`.

```dockerfile
FROM alpine:3.20
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=mainland_token \
    grep -q '^KP-' /run/secrets/mainland_token \
    && echo token-ok > /opt/uplink-status
CMD ["cat", "/opt/uplink-status"]
```
```bash
docker build -t kestrel/uplink:1.0 \
  --secret id=mainland_token,src=secrets/mainland.token .
```

files.content:
FROM alpine:3.20
ARG MAINLAND_TOKEN
RUN echo "$MAINLAND_TOKEN" | grep -q '^KP-' && echo token-ok > /opt/uplink-status
CMD ["cat", "/opt/uplink-status"]

validation.description: The Dockerfile uses `--mount=type=secret,id=mainland_token` and no longer declares `ARG MAINLAND_TOKEN`
The build consumed the token: `/opt/uplink-status` in the image contains `token-ok`
The token does not appear in `docker history --no-trunc kestrel/uplink:1.0`

params.command: if docker image inspect kestrel/uplink:1.0 | grep -q KP-4e9b27d1- || docker run --rm --entrypoint sh kestrel/uplink:1.0 -c 'grep -rsq KP-4e9b27d1- /etc /opt /root /home /tmp /var /usr /app'; then echo LEAK; else echo CLEAN; fi

validation.description: The token is not stored in the image metadata (env, labels) or anywhere in its filesystem

solution:
cat > Dockerfile <<'EOF'
FROM alpine:3.20
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=mainland_token \
    grep -q '^KP-' /run/secrets/mainland_token \
    && echo token-ok > /opt/uplink-status
CMD ["cat", "/opt/uplink-status"]
EOF
debrief: A `--build-arg` or `ENV` is written into the image for everyone who can pull it, while a secret mount exists only for the one `RUN` step that asks for it. Pro tip: `--secret id=x,env=VAR` reads the secret from an environment variable instead of a file.
